The predicted within-subject eﬀects were found.
For Colour cues, attentional bias was drawn
towards the colour cue on which the target was presented in the previous trial. This replicated the previous ﬁnding on colour cues and carryover

for negative facial expressions, as in previous

expression was found following target-on-negative

Fang et al. (2008) extended Murray et al.’s (2002)
results by demonstrating that in addition to the clear

authors (F. Fang, personal communication, August

labeled LOC in fact only contained what we have
deﬁned as the more posterior shape selective region LO.

p , 0.001). It is also likely that the more anterior shape
selective region on the ventral surface that we have
labeled pFs corresponds to what Fang et al. labeled
temporal object areas (TOA). Although there is a
similar pattern of results in pFs to that found in LO
(see Figure 5) these are not signiﬁcant, F(15, 150) ¼
0.74, p ¼ 0.7, a pattern broadly consistent with the
results of Fang et al.

Although our earlier study (Murray et al., 2002)
included a condition using a similar bistable “translating
diamond,” the current study represents a significant
advance in methodology and analysis. Here we used an
independently defined, retinotopically specific localizer
for V1. Thus, we are confident that the modulations in the
fMRI signal that we observed occurred in the retinotopic
representation of the stimulus and not in immediately
adjacent retinotopic regions (e.g., artifacts due to “bloodflow steal”). In addition, due to limited slice-selection, our
previous report using the translating diamond only made
measurements in V1. Here, using an independent localizer
for the LOC, we show significant changes that inversely
reflect the pattern of activity observed in V1. Finally, the
current study employs event-related averaging that characterizes the temporal dynamics and the magnitudes of V1
and LOC changes in more detail than our previous report.

expert_opinion.location: Introduction, Current Study, Results (Moderating Analyses), Discussion, and References, line 1
expert_opinion.quote: In the FHF pilot study we found that (1) severity of neglect did not moderate outcomes, suggesting that children with severe neglect histories were just as likely to benefit from the intervention as those with less severe neglect histories ( Taussig, Culhane, Garrido, Knudtson, & Petrenko, 2013 ) but that (2) level of risk (i.e., exposure to ACEs) did moderate some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress and dissociative symptoms), such that maltreated children exposed to a relatively higher number of ACEs did not experience the same reduction in trauma symptoms as children exposed to fewer adversities ( Weiler & Taussig, 2017 ).
expert_opinion.reason: Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work. Weiler & Taussig (2017) (10.1080/15374416.2017.1295379, Journal of Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology) is a distinct 2017 study reporting that baseline exposure to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) moderated FHF intervention effects on trauma symptoms such that youth with fewer ACEs experienced stronger reductions in posttraumatic stress symptoms. In the Current Study section, the authors formulate their sole directional a priori moderation hypothesis specifically to retest this finding; in Moderating Analyses they test the ACEs x treatment interaction on T2 outcomes; and in Discussion they explicitly state that their results 'replicated our earlier finding that children exposed to relatively fewer ACEs tended to benefit more on some outcomes (i.e., posttraumatic stress symptoms and quality of life)'. Shipped row 754 (Taussig, 2012, 10.1037/e522512014-027) and target_index 0 (Taussig & Culhane, 2010) predated this 2017 moderation study by 5 to 7 years and reported main RCT effects rather than the Weiler & Taussig (2017) ACEs moderation finding.
